subject: Request: private hosting operational assumptions and SLA exceptions for Silverpine
messages:
From: Liam Carver <liam.carver@silverpine.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Request: Private hosting SLA exceptions for Silverpine

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to move ahead with Redwood Private installed in our on-prem environment, but before we sign the commitment we need to capture a few operational assumptions in the contract so our security and ops teams can accept the deployment. Specifically: 

- Network responsibility: our WAN and edge routers are under Silverpine control. We need explicit carveouts for network-caused latency/jitter and transit outages (we can provide visibility into our edge metrics).
- KMS and key custody: keys will be in our HSM; any key-usage latency that contributes to token generation latency should not count toward Redwood SLOs.
- Maintenance windows: we need the ability to schedule maintenance on our colo network that can affect availability and want that excluded from Redwood uptime calculations if we notify you 72h in advance.
- Observability: to troubleshoot production incidents we agree to provide syslogs and flow records; in return we need clear telemetry requirements (what Redwood needs to collect) and minimal data retention for debug traces.

Can Redwood provide a short Operational Assumptions appendix that we can attach to the MSA? If possible we want a mutual action plan and a sample runbook showing the observability hooks you need (metrics, traces, and the minimum packet/flow detail). We can target signing by Nov 10th if we can agree on language by Nov 5th.

Attached is our network topology diagram and a short list of compliance questions from our security team (attachment: silverpine-topology.pdf).

Best,
Liam Carver
Head of Infrastructure
Silverpine Research

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Liam Carver <liam.carver@silverpine.io>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T08:24:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private hosting SLA exceptions for Silverpine

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear note and the topology. We can absolutely document a short Operational Assumptions appendix to sit alongside the MSA. To move quickly I propose we start with three focused sections:

1) Shared responsibility matrix: call out "Redwood-managed" vs "Customer-managed" owns for network, KMS, DNS, and colo power.
2) Telemetry & evidence: minimal telemetry Redwood requires (latency histograms, kv-cache hit/miss, request IDs, and optional flow logs) and acceptable evidence formats for network incidents (NetFlow, BGP session logs).
3) SLA carveouts & maintenance: explicit exclusion for customer-controlled network outages, agreed notice windows, and a joint incident postmortem commitment.

I'll attach a one-page draft appendix (redwood-private-ops-assumptions-draft-v1.pdf) with suggested wording for those areas. Marcus and Priya are looped in for legal and platform implications. Two quick asks on our side:

- Can Silverpine confirm the KMS provider (vendor/model) and whether the HSM is reachable over the local network only? That affects our fallback behavior.
- Can you share the specific telemetry retention window you need for debug (e.g., 72h / 7 days)?

If you want, we can do a 30-minute call Wed (Nov 4) to iterate the wording; otherwise we'll update the draft and share an editable DocuSign-ready appendix.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-ops-assumptions-draft-v1.pdf

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: FW: Request: Private hosting SLA exceptions for Silverpine — draft language and risk tiers

Team — forwarding Liam's asks and the attached topology. Quick summary and proposed approach: 

- Risk tiering: label customer-controlled network issues as Tier C (customer responsibility) and exclude those incidents from Redwood uptime calculations; include a small carveout for transitive latency when KMS calls cross customer edge (if KMS latency > X ms then that token latency is excluded).
- Telemetry: platform needs 72h of high-fidelity traces (request ID, model + tokens, timestamp, backend latency), with aggregated histograms stored 90 days for SLA reporting. For network evidence we accept NetFlow for 7 days. Naomi, can security confirm acceptance of NetFlow for incident proof?
- Legal: Priya, please review the draft appendix for contract language that references runbook obligations and notice windows (we suggested 72h notice for planned maint). Also note SLA math: when an incident is marked Tier C we will not count that downtime toward % uptime.

Action items: Priya to provide redline by EOD Nov 4. Marcus to confirm platform telemetry feasibility and whether we can toggle latency attribution per customer KMS reachability. I'll coordinate a final call with Silverpine on Nov 5 if EOD redlines are ready.

Quoted message below for context.

—Jonas

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@silverpine.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam Carver <liam.carver@silverpine.io>
Date: 2026-11-06T14:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private hosting operational assumptions and SLA exceptions for Silverpine

Jonas, Priya, Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft appendix. We reviewed the language with security and legal. A few notes: 

- Silverpine accepts the Tier C carveout for customer-operated WAN/edge. We will provide NetFlow evidence and calendar-based maintenance notices of >=72h.
- KMS: our HSM (Thales nShield) is on-prem and only reachable from our internal VLANs; we agree Redwood should exclude KMS-induced token latency from Redwood SLOs when the HSM response time exceeds 50ms.
- Telemetry: we can provide 72h of full traces; 90-day aggregated histograms are fine. We request a scoped redaction agreement for any PII in traces.

We've signed the amendment and uploaded the DocuSign package (see attachment: silverpine-amendment-docusign.pdf). If everything looks good on your end we'll proceed with the on-prem rollout week of Nov 15.

Next steps from our side: please send the final appendix as a DocuSign envelope and confirm the go-live checklist (runbook handshake, onboarding playbook, and a short tech workshop).

Best,
Ellen Park
VP, Security & Compliance
Silverpine Research

Attachment: silverpine-amendment-docusign.pdf
Link: https://docusign.com/embedded/sign/abc123def
